title: Teachers: Professor Delmar, Chris Kelly and Paul Barnes
summary: Howard studied with Professor Delmar and Chris; learned reading and arranging from Paul Barnes at La Vida.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: See there was something else I was going to ask you about your teacher. Whatever you really get into that.

Oh Professor Delmar, he was a professor, but I'd taken lessons quite a while with him. In fact most of the fellas did at that time. Where did he live? Well he had lived in a city but he was from some part of the country I just remember.
But what part of the city? Do you remember his exact account?
Well most of the time he used to be on Ramport and culminated at a pressing shop, Professor
Pritchett.
You remember that? He'd be right in there most of the time. That's where he used to be. I see.
And that's where you'd get him, huh?
Well no, he'd come to the house. He'd come to the house.
Do you remember his first name? No, I just remember that. Oh we called him first. Yeah we won't ask Pritchett.
Yeah you can ask him, he knows for sure. Professor Delmar.
That's right. And you said you had Chris at some point.
Well Chris started me off, yeah. He turned the horn and I went to him for quite a while. I started first after I'd formed the band. You see.
What did he teach you exactly? Reading?
Well reading, reading. I could read pretty close.
I didn't know whether Chris was a reader or not.
Well Chris was like the average guy it was, you might say. But some don't give a guy credit.
You know what I mean?
Some would say different things.
Would he read on the stand?

Well he didn't play no arrangement or nothing like Papa Celestan and he'd keep up with the late music. The late music mostly I'd hear him play would be maybe the introduction and the chorus of a song and like that.
So he'd talk about the sheet music then, huh?
No he would have orchestration.
Well he'd get an orchestration and just.
Well they'd have some time, they'd have good readers, would be with him like Yank, Yank was a good reader, different stuff like that. Well he'd, you know, get them together. That's right.
How long did you go to Professor Delmarine?

Well I was on and off with Chris for about five years or something, let's say something like that. Off and off. Sometimes he would leave and go out of town, go someplace in the country where he'd teach the rest of the country. And I learned a lot from Paul at the La Vida. You see, he's a good reader. Louis DeMann, he liked me, I liked him very much.
Well he was more than just a reader, didn't he?
Well he could play a few numbers or get along already a few numbers by a head, but mostly he was a reader.
Yeah but I mean he could do arrangements and everything too.
Yeah, oh yeah.
Because the Eureka played some of his stuff and the Tuxedo both. Yeah.
Well I have a lot of manuscript paper that he'd buy sheet music to keep up with all the ladies, and every time he'd get something he'd fix it and bring it down to me.
